mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for three consecutive months signals a robust residential investment cycle, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of HOUST monthly change > 5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 6-month averages indicates a labor market expansion with slack, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 6-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 10% for two consecutive quarters signals elevated household savings and reduced consumption, which dampens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS quarterly change > 10% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS quarterly change > 10% for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).
